title: Why the energy sector must plan for post-quantum cyber security now - Semiwiki
gist: SemiWiki (PQShield category) summarizes a WEF piece by Ali El Kaafarani arguing that energy operators must plan post-quantum cryptography migration now because grid assets last decades and are hard to upgrade. Cites UK NCSC 2028/2031/2035 milestones, a June 2026 US policy, and a December 2025 Polish attack on 30+ wind/solar farms.

themes.theme: Long-lived grid assets vs quantum risk

insights.claim: Energy companies should begin preparing for post-quantum cryptography now because power infrastructure lasts decades while replacing its security can take years, so equipment bought today may still run when quantum advances break current cryptography.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Creates near-term procurement demand for PQC-capable grid equipment and security IP.
insights.locator: In a September 2026 World Economic Forum

insights.claim: The call is for a planned PQC transition, not a claim that quantum computers are already breaking power-grid security.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Demand is driven by planning timelines, not an imminent break; adoption will be gradual.
insights.quote: The article’s call is for a planned transition, not a claim that quantum computers are already breaking power-grid security.

insights.claim: Grid PQC migration is unusually hard because many components have limited computing capacity, cannot easily go offline and require extensive testing; the systems hardest to secure are often hardest to replace.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Favors lightweight PQC implementations for constrained embedded devices (e.g., PQShield-type IP).
insights.quote: the systems that are hardest to secure are often the hardest to replace

insights.claim: A December 2025 incident in Poland saw attackers target more than 30 wind and solar farms, a manufacturing company and a major power plant, illustrating how connected energy systems offer many routes in.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Renewables build-out widens grid cyber attack surface, supporting OT security spend.

insights.claim: AI is a reason to move faster on security since it helps attackers find weaknesses, though it is distinct from the quantum threat to cryptography.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-enabled attacks accelerate security testing cadence and budgets.
insights.locator: El Kaafarani also points to artificial intelligence

insights.claim: The UK National Cyber Security Centre set milestones for PQC discovery and initial planning by 2028, early priority migration by 2031 and completion by 2035.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Hard dates convert PQC from optional to budgeted spend for critical infrastructure.
insights.locator: There is a policy timetable as well

insights.claim: A June 2026 US policy directs federal systems toward post-quantum standards and supports critical infrastructure operators with transitions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: US policy adds demand pull for PQC products in the 2026-2035 window.
insights.locator: There is a policy timetable as well

insights.claim: PQC planning should start with a cryptographic inventory and build crypto-agility questions into procurement, supplier assessments and scheduled replacements.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Suppliers lacking crypto-agility roadmaps risk losing grid procurement deals.
